title: The Machinery Has No Board
eyebrow: Every card and every file now sits with the project that owns it, and nothing of the shared machinery stands in the racing project — not a copy, not a pointer.

content.lead: 614 cards were open on the racing board and 194 of them were not about the racing game. They have moved.

blocks.label: Two cards carry the board's name here, and neither is work
blocks.text: One is the merge lock every board keeps. The other is the ticket for this job itself, sitting in your column for you to sign off. Nothing else on the racing board is about the board.

blocks.label: You were right about the cancelled ones — twice
blocks.text: Bringing a card back put its status right and left everything else the cancel had written: two tags, a line in its notes, and a leftover placeholder card. Your screen draws its Cancelled column from the tags, not the status, so 28 racing cards — the tyre, the leaf veins, the sun glint, the lens ghosts — were live work to every tool on this machine and dropped work to you. All 30 across the three boards are put right, and the board's health check now refuses that state: a card that is live and tagged cancelled at once makes it exit red and names the card.

content.label: Why it refills
content.lead: Three causes, all mechanical, and the third is the one that matters.

rows.title: The racing project still names the board as one of its own systems
rows.note: Its declaration lists the board among the subjects a card here may be about, so filing one is accepted rather than refused.

rows.title: There is nowhere else to file it
rows.note: The shared machinery is a repository with no board at all. An agent that finds a fault in a shared tool has exactly one board within reach, and the rules say a fault must be filed before the turn ends.

rows.title: The machinery's own changes are unwatched
rows.note: Because it has no board, none of its checks fire there. Its last four changes were committed with no card of their own, no review by anyone who did not write them, and card numbers borrowed from the racing project. It is the only checkout on this machine where work lands unwatched — and that is the same hole, seen from the other side.

content.label: What is still not moved
content.lead: Nothing. The last of it moved today.

rows: The shared home. The folder that stood in this project is gone, and every mention of it names the shared one outright
The shared home, wired once for this machine rather than once per project
The shared home. The tables it measures against — this project's own component boundaries, concerns, constants, cycles and floors — stayed, because they are this project's design
The five documentation and comment checks

Still this project's own. They are written against the two languages this project is built in and against its own rules file, and moving them means teaching the shared home which languages each project writes

blocks.label: The specialist helpers here are right where they belong
blocks.text: The car, track, tree and plant researchers, the render checks and the bug isolator are subject knowledge, not machinery. They stay, and that was the line you approved.

content.label: What changes if this goes ahead
content.lead: Your board is the racing game again, and the machinery answers to the same standard as everything else.

items: The racing board holds 444 open cards and every one is about the racing game.
Filing a card here that belongs somewhere else is refused by name, and the refusal prints the command that files it on the right board — so the board stops refilling instead of being drained again.
A change to the shared machinery now gets a card, a review by someone who did not write it, and a close that has to be earned. Its last six changes got none of those.
No copy and no pointer of the machinery stands in any project: one file, one home, checked by a tool that goes red if a copy appears.
A move that cannot close the old card now refuses instead of reporting success — the way two cards ended up open on two boards at once, which you saw.
The board's own health check runs again in all three projects; since the tools moved out it had been asking a folder that is not a board and dying.

decisions.title: The shared machinery becomes a project in its own right, with its own declaration and its own checks
decisions.why: It is the only checkout on this machine where a change lands with no card, no review and no close. Its last four changes borrowed the racing project's card numbers, which is how 172 cards ended up on the wrong board. Making it a project is one short declaration; the alternative is teaching every check a permanent exception.

decisions.title: The board stops being one of the racing project's own systems
decisions.why: While it stays on that list, filing a shared-tools fault here is legal and costs nothing, so the next few hours refill whatever a move drains. Removing it turns the leak into a refusal that names where the card should go.

decisions.title: Cards move by who owns the thing they describe, and nothing a live session is holding is touched
decisions.why: The tools go to the machinery, the screen faults go to the beads board, the racing game keeps the rest. Cards held right now stay where they are and move when their session lets go — a card yanked out from under a working session is worse than a card on the wrong board.

decisions.title: The documentation and comment checks are craft and move; the part of the push check that is about this project's own build targets stays
decisions.why: A comment that reads as a diary and prose that restates the code beside it are faults in any language, in any project. The submodule half of the push check is the same. The half that names this project's build targets is not.

decisions.title: The quality suite stays unmerged until the session that owns those files says it is finished
decisions.why: That session has a guard, a review and a write-up still landing in the same files. Merging under it means the same file is written twice by two sessions, which is exactly the collision the single merge slot exists to prevent.

decisions.title: The move is a tool, not 198 cards edited by hand
decisions.why: The first move was classified card by card and never ran. A tool that takes a list of ids and moves them whole — body, notes, tags, links, priority — is repeatable, reviewable, and can be run without touching anything first. There will be a second move; this project's rule is that the second manual inspection becomes a tool.

decisions.title: Two refusals, not one
decisions.why: Taking the board off the racing project's list of subjects stops the obvious half. It cannot stop the other half: 52 of these cards arrived tagged as tooling, and the racing game has real tooling of its own, so that word cannot be refused. The second refusal reads the evidence instead — a card whose evidence names a place inside another project is refused and told where to go. That one is the difference between closing the leak and draining it again.

decisions.title: No pointers either — every reference names the shared home outright
decisions.why: Your call. A pointer still reads as a folder in the project and still invites someone to edit it there. Ninety files named the old paths; they all name the real one now, and the shared gates are wired once for the machine instead of once per project.

next.if_nothing: Nothing breaks. The five documentation checks stay this project's own, so the beads screen's prose is held to a lower standard than this project's.

steps.step: The documentation and comment checks start applying to every project of yours, so the beads screen's prose is held to the standard this project already meets
